sources.title: Kumaon Kingdom
sources.note: Katyuri principality (7th century, "Around 700 CE" under Vasu Dev), Chand dynasty from the 8th century at Champawat, capital Almora from 1563, Ratna Chand unified Kumaon around 1450, Gyan Chand invaded Garhwal in 1699, Rohilla invasion of 1742, Nepal invaded in 1791, Treaty of Sugauli (1816 on the page).

sources.title: Baz Bahadur Chand
sources.note: Reign 1638-1678; army sent to Garhwal in 1654-55; Mughal army sent to Kumaon in 1665; Aurangzeb's army captured the Terai in October 1665; captured the fort of Taklakot in 1670; pardoned in October 1673; abdicated 1678; died at Almora in 1680.

sources.title: Treaty of Sugauli
sources.note: Ochterlony pushed the Nepalese out of Garhwal and Kumaon across the Kali in 1815; signed 4 March 1816; the Kali became the western boundary of Nepal.

notes: Three pages opened (Kumaon Kingdom, Baz Bahadur Chand, Treaty of Sugauli); Ali Mohammed Khan Rohilla was opened and is silent on Kumaon (the first fetch of the misspelt URL Ali_Mohammad_Khan_Rohilla returned url_not_found). Conflicts: Established 600 (infobox) against "Around 700 CE" and the 8th century for the Chands (text); the Gorkha invasion 1791 (page) against 1790; the cession to the British 1816 (page) against 1815 (Sugauli page and nepal dossier: Almora fell on 27 April 1815). The nepal dossier (sa-05-f) already carries gain kumaon-kingdom in 1791. The Terai events of 1638, 1665 and 1673 rest on two pages that disagree in kind (reinstated authority, undated, against a Mughal capture in October 1665); the rohilkhand-state dossier carries the matching gain of 1742. british-empire (sa-06) should record the gain of Kumaon in 1815 (from nepal), after the end of this dossier. Gazetteer lacks Kumaon, Champawat, Almora, Baijnath, Kashipur and Rudrapur as names; Natural Earth admin1 Uttarakhand and coordinate circles are used.
